reason: The section applies listed intestacy rules to a woman dying intestate through substitutions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Intestate distribution for a woman

focusSelections.evidenceText: distributed in the same proportions and in the same manner

proposedGroups.reason: The substitutions change widow to widower and related pronouns in listed sections.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the statutory substitutions for distributing the estate of a woman dying intestate.

reason: The target contains only a repealed section note and has no current operative study content.
The section vests mortgaged real property in the personal representative on death absent testamentary disposition.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Devolution of mortgaged real property to personal representative
proposedGroups.reason: The property remains subject to like rights, equities, obligations, trusts, and powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize how real property vested by way of mortgage devolves on death.

reason: The Easements Act section creates different consequences after thirty and sixty years of enjoying profits or benefits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Thirty-year enjoyment protects profit or benefit claims from ancient-origin defeat
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection prevents defeat based only on lack of time-immemorial origin after thirty years uninterrupted enjoyment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the effect of thirty years enjoyment on a profit or benefit claim.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Sixty-year enjoyment makes profit or benefit rights indefeasible except written consent
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection makes the right absolute after sixty years unless enjoyment was under express deed or written consent.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the sixty-year rule and written-consent exception for profit or benefit claims.

reason: The general easement section uses separate twenty-year and forty-year thresholds.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Twenty-year enjoyment protects general easement claims from ancient-origin defeat
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection protects claims to ways, easements, watercourses, and water use after twenty years enjoyment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the effect of twenty years enjoyment on general easement and water-use claims.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Forty-year enjoyment makes general easement rights indefeasible except written consent
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection makes the right absolute after forty years unless enjoyment was under express deed or written consent.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the forty-year rule and written-consent exception.

reason: The section fixes how prescription periods and interruptions are measured for sections 1 and 2.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Computing easement periods and interruptions

focusSelections.evidenceText: period next before a suit or action

proposedGroups.reason: Interruption counts only after notice and one year of submission or acquiescence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine how easement periods are measured and when an interruption counts.

reason: The pleading section has separate rules for general allegations, enjoyment pleadings, and special pleading of exceptions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: General allegation and evidence for easement claims
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection preserves general pleading and admits sections 1 to 3 matters to sustain or rebut it.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize when a general allegation of right is sufficient.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Pleading enjoyment as of right instead of time immemorial
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection allows pleading enjoyment as of right for statutory periods rather than time immemorial.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify how a claimant may plead enjoyment for statutory periods.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Special pleading of exceptions, disabilities, agreements, or other matters
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection requires exceptions and similar matters to be specially alleged instead of raised under general denial.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the requirement to specially plead matters answering an easement claim.

reason: The section bars presumptions from enjoyment periods shorter than those stated in the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No presumption from shorter enjoyment periods

focusSelections.evidenceText: no presumption shall be allowed or made

proposedGroups.reason: The rule applies to profits, ways, watercourses, and other easements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize that shorter-than-statutory enjoyment does not support a presumption.

reason: The section excludes specified disabilities and abated litigation time when computing periods unless the right is already absolute.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Excluded time in computing prescription periods

focusSelections.evidenceText: shall be excluded in the computation of the periods

proposedGroups.reason: The exclusions include mental incompetence, minority, life tenancy, and certain pending actions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify which periods are excluded when computing prescription periods.

reason: The target excludes enjoyment during life terms or long terms of years from the forty-year calculation in defined circumstances.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Excluding long lease terms from forty-year easement calculations

focusSelections.evidenceText: term of years exceeding three years

proposedGroups.reason: The exclusion applies when a reversioner resists within three years after the term ends.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the term exclusion for forty-year easement or water-use claims.

reason: The section prevents acquisition of a right to block adjoining construction merely through window light and air use.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No easement for light or air from overlooking windows

focusSelections.evidenceText: mere use of light and air through the windows

proposedGroups.reason: The rule preserves rights acquired before April 10, 1875.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the statutory exclusion for light or air through windows.

reason: The target bars prescriptive easements for wires or cables attached to or passing over land or buildings.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No prescriptive easement for wires or cables

focusSelections.evidenceText: wire or cable attached to land or a building

proposedGroups.reason: The rule prevents past and future acquisition by prescription.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the rule barring prescriptive easements for wires or cables.

reason: The section protects local-government water supply lands from prescriptive easement and limitation-title claims unless completed before acquisition.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No prescriptive rights against local-government water supply lands

focusSelections.evidenceText: water supply of a local government

proposedGroups.reason: The protected lands include lakes, reservoirs, dams, overflow, pipes, and related water-control lands.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize protection for local-government water supply lands against prescription claims.

reason: The definitions section frames electronic information, electronic signatures, information, and legal requirements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Electronic Transactions Act definitions
proposedGroups.reason: The target supplies core definitions for applying the Electronic Transactions Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify key definitions for electronic information and signatures under the Act.

reason: The target clarifies that legal requirements include both obligations and consequences.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Legal requirements may create obligations or consequences
proposedGroups.reason: The rule covers legal consequences for doing or not doing something.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the scope of legal requirements covered by the Act.

reason: The target states the Act purpose as facilitating use and acceptance of electronic information.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Purpose of facilitating electronic information

focusSelections.evidenceText: facilitate the use and acceptance of electronic information

proposedGroups.reason: The purpose applies to persons who wish to use electronic information.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the stated purpose of the Electronic Transactions Act.

reason: The section makes the Act permissive rather than compulsory.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No requirement to use or accept electronic information

focusSelections.evidenceText: requires a person to use or accept electronic information

proposedGroups.reason: No person is required by the Act itself to use or accept electronic information.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize that the Act does not compel electronic information use or acceptance.

reason: The section gives priority to other express electronic-information Acts and permits regulatory exclusions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application limits where other Acts or regulations govern electronic information
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections address conflict with other Acts and exclusions by regulation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine when the Electronic Transactions Act gives way to another Act or regulation.
